In summary, our research is concerned with
the determination of all relativistic wave equations which are Poincaré and Θ invariant.

the determination of the most general form of relativistic wave equation for a particle of arbitrary mass m, spin s, and charge q, which is invariant under the combined operation of the Lorentze group and the discrete operation Θ = TCP.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most general equations for free particles are those invariant under the Pioncare group and the operation Θ ≡ TPC.
there are only three types of wave equations for free spin- s particles, each of which is invariant under the full Poincare group, the combined operation Θ, and the individual operations T, C, or P.

the only equations of motion for free particles of mass m and spin (or angular momentum) s which are invariant under all the operations of the Poincaré and the combined operation of Θ = TCP, are the equations of Dirac, Weyl, Majorana, Rarita–Schwinger, and Fierz–Pauli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a unique wave equation for each pair of values of the mass and the spin.

there is only one wave equation for each spin s, namely that given by the Dirac equation for the case s = 1/2, the Rarita–Schwinger equation for the case of s = 3/2, the Fierz–Pauli–Kofink–van Dantzig equation for the case that s = 2, and the Bargmann–Wigner equation for arbitrary s.

all such equations are of the standard form and can be classified into three categories: (i) those invariant under Θ, but not under T, C or P; (ii) those invariant under T, but not under Θ, C, or P; and (iii) those invariant under C, but not under P, Θ, or T.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the standard form for wave equations of free particles of arbitrary spin is not only the most convenient form for the derivation of such equations, but also the most convenient form in which to investigate their invariance under the Poincaré group.
the TCP invariance is a necessary condition for the invariance of the wave equations for free massive particles under the combined operation Θ.
the standard form is a natural and convenient starting point for the construction of relativistic wave equation for particles of arbitrary mass and spin.
